claims.claim: CRC COVERAGE GAP (M-36 counterexample constructed, contradicting the 'torn tail only' framing): the crc32 covers seq||payload ONLY — the leading u32 totalLen length field is NOT covered by any checksum. Append computes Crc32Of(frame.Slice(LenSize + CrcSize, SeqSize + payload.Length)), i.e. it starts AFTER the length field. A corrupted-but-plausible length (the only validation is totalLen >= 12 && totalLen <= 1<<30 at :114/:234) misframes the read; the crc then mismatches and the reader yield-breaks. So a single flipped bit in a length field is not reported as a length corruption — it is silently reclassified as a torn tail.

So a corrupt record in the MIDDLE of a non-final segment makes replay silently stop, and every good record in that segment's tail AND in every LATER segment is never yielded. claims.claim: THE SAME UNBOUNDED-GROWTH DEFECT IS IN IdempotentSink, AND IT IS WORSE. IdempotentSink never calls _wal.CheckpointAsync (its only WAL uses are the ctor, ReplayAsync(0), Append, CommitAsync, DisposeAsync), so its WAL is never pruned; on open it replays from 0 and folds EVERY record ever delivered into _seen (HashSet<string>) AND into _records (List<(string, byte[])>) — retaining every delivered payload in memory forever. claims.claim: SECOND DOC/CODE DISAGREEMENT (doc quoted): IDurableMailbox.TryWrite is documented '(no durable side-effect on reject)'. In DurableMailbox.TryWrite the WAL Append happens BEFORE the channel publish; if _channel.Writer.TryWrite returns false (e.g. after the writer was completed on dispose) the method releases the slot and returns false — a REJECT — but the appended WAL record already exists and will be replayed on the next open. claims.claim: THE CHECKPOINT FILE ITSELF IS NOT POWER-LOSS DURABLE, and its failure is swallowed. WriteCheckpoint writes checkpoint.json.tmp with File.WriteAllText and File.Move(overwrite: true) — the code's own comment hedges 'atomic-ish replace'. ReadCheckpoint likewise returns 0 on ANY exception (including a parse failure of a corrupted checkpoint). Failure direction is safe (replay more, at-least-once) but it is silent: a lost checkpoint degrades to a full replay from 0 with no signal.

claims.claim: A REAL, NAMED DURABILITY DEFECT WAS ALREADY FOUND AND FIXED HERE — the contiguous-low-water ack. DurableMailbox.AckAsync keeps out-of-order acks in a SortedSet (_ackedAhead) and advances _ackedLowWater only while the next seq is acked, so the checkpoint never passes an unacked hole. The in-code comment states the prior implementation ('the old interlocked-max ack') checkpointed past out-of-order unacked messages and silently skipped them on replay, and names it a lineage defect. EVIDENCE VALUE: this is the codebase's own record that its checkpoint arithmetic has been wrong before in precisely the silent-skip direction.

claims.claim: THE BOUNDED-CAPACITY GUARANTEE IS SUSPENDED FOR RECOVERED ITEMS — an unbounded memory burst on restart. DurableMailbox.OpenAsync accumulates ALL replayed records into a List<Envelope<T>> and then TryWrites every one into the UNBOUNDED channel without consuming producer slots; ReadAllAsync/TryRead only release a slot when env.Seq > _replayHighWater. The doc states this intentionally ('recovered (replayed) items burst through without consuming slots'). Consequence for a high-cycle-count budget: a node that crashed with a large unacked backlog materializes that entire backlog in RAM at open, unbounded by Capacity — the very bound OpenAsync fail-loud REFUSES to run without (':58-59 unbounded mailboxes are refused).

claims.claim: CATEGORY: EXISTS AND COULD BE WIRED (but is NOT wired today) — the fix for the headline risk is small and local. IWriteAheadLog.CheckpointAsync + FileWriteAheadLog.PruneConsumedSegments are fully implemented and proven in use by DurableMailbox; nothing prevents DurableExecutor and IdempotentSink from calling CheckpointAsync on their own WALs. What is MISSING is the arithmetic for a safe consumed-frontier on a journal whose whole history is load-bearing for state-fold and dedup: pruning the commit journal is only safe once state is snapshotted, and pruning the sink's WAL is only safe once the dedup key set has a retention bound. So the segment-pruning PRIMITIVE exists; the SAFETY FRONTIER that would let these two callers use it does not exist in my sources.
